key_insight: DT-DRO uses held-out calibration data to reshape the ambiguity set geometry so distributionally robust optimization better matches observed predictive errors and avoids excessive conservatism.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to make robust decision systems less overcautious and more reliable when deployed under model misspecification, especially in high-stakes applications like energy systems.
method: Uses the conditional probability integral transform (PIT) to diagnose systematic probability misallocation.
Converts the diagnostic signal into an outcome-level transport that adjusts both the ambiguity-set center and the ground cost.
Derives a computationally tractable dual reformulation with valid ambiguity radii and risk guarantees.
evidence_signal: The paper reports synthetic experiments and a power-outage case study showing improved decision quality, especially under structural and tail misspecification.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of held-out calibration data, and the added calibration/transport step may be sensitive to estimation error.
paper_title: Calibrating Ambiguity Set via Diagnostic Transport for Distributionally Robust Optimization
